## Provider & keys

<!-- parity: /provider /providers -->

User file, top-level keys:

```yaml
provider: openai-completions   # openai-completions | anthropic | google | dial | minimax | zai
model: openai/gpt-4o-mini      # model id sent to the provider
baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
```

Saved custom endpoints (the `/provider custom` flow persists here):

```yaml
customProviders:
  - name: my-llama             # non-empty, unique
    apiType: openai            # openai | anthropic | google | dial | openrouter
    baseUrl: http://localhost:11434/v1
    modelId: llama3            # non-empty
    keyName: MY_KEY            # optional: env/secure-store NAME, never the value
    authMethod: apiKey         # apiKey | sso | jwt (optional)
```

Applies: a direct YAML edit takes effect at next boot. `/provider <name>
[baseUrl] [token]` switches the live session too.
Keys: never inline values (rule 2). Key resolution order — environment value,
then endpoint-scoped secure-store entry (`FA_KEY_<HOST>`), then legacy env-name
store entries. `/key set|delete` manages the store and has NO config.yaml
equivalent — that is deliberate.

## Models & roles

<!-- parity: /model /models /model-edit -->

User file. The active model is the `model:` top-level key (above). Optional
sections:

```yaml
roles:                         # intent → ordered fallback chain
  default:
    - openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4
    - provider: openai         # or a map entry:
      model: gpt-4o
      apiKeyName: OPENAI_API_KEY   # optional; also baseUrl, contextWindow, maxTokens
      connectTimeoutMs: 45000       # optional per-entry watchdog override
      streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000  #   (slow local model recipe, see below)
      thinkingLevel: high       # optional: minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max
                                # (xhigh/max fold to high) — reasoning request
  smol: [openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini]   # roles: default, smol, slow, plan, subagent, memory
modelOverrides:                # scope chains to path prefixes
  - path: ~/work/acme
    roles:
      plan: [anthropic/claude-opus-4-5]
retry:                         # chain fallback policy
  retriesPerEntry: 2           # + baseDelayMs, maxBackoffMs, maxWaitMs, keyBackoffMs
providerTimeouts:              # GLOBAL fallback: only these two keys
  connectTimeoutMs: 180000
  streamIdleTimeoutMs: 300000
agent:                         # strict: contextWindowCap (issue #273) +
                               # foreground-call budget keys (issue #1786)
  contextWindowCap: 262144     # owner context cap; min 16384 = the compaction reserve
  foregroundCallBudgetSeconds: 600  # foreground tool-call budget B in seconds;
                                    # int > 0, default 600 (10 min)
  foregroundCallAutoConvert: offer  # rung-1 behavior at B/2: offer (default, ask)
                                    # or auto (convert to background unattended)
images:                        # session image registry (strict): send-once
  registry: true               # kill switch — false = byte-for-byte legacy
  maxPerRequest: 20            # per-request unique-image cap (default 20)
models:                        # media slots + named custom models
  slots:
    vision:
      providerKind: openai-completions
      baseUrl: https://api.openai.com/v1
      modelId: gpt-4o
      apiKeyName: OPENAI_API_KEY
  custom:
    fast:
      provider: openai
      baseUrl: https://api.openai.com/v1
      model: gpt-4o-mini
      contextWindow: 128000    # + maxTokens, input
```

Scoped provider timeouts (issue #1554): `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`
are valid on `roles:` chain entries, `customProviders:` entries, and
`models.custom:` entries. Per field, the first level that declares a value
wins — **role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry >
global `providerTimeouts:` > built-in default** (connect 180 s, idle 300 s;
hard sanity bound 1 h). Configs without the keys behave byte-identically.
Slow-local-model recipe: on the role entry that pins the local endpoint set
only `streamIdleTimeoutMs` ≈ 2× the model's worst silent prefill stretch —
the cloud providers in the same config keep the global watchdog untouched,
and the stall line names the override (`idle window 1800s (role default
override)`) so a wide window never reads as a hang.

Media slot names (exact): `imageGeneration`, `audioTts`, `musicGeneration`,
`videoGeneration`, `vision`, `transcription`. A slot without an override falls
back to the main connection.

The `images:` section has no settings-hub editor — the registry is runtime
state, not a persisted setting: `/images` (CLI) and the app's image-drop
chip/panel render the shared window/cap/drop projection, and the drop
notice model is latched (one notice per meaningful change, issue #1889;
see `docs/images.md`). The three keys above are the whole config surface,
applied at next boot.

CLI equivalents: `/model <id>` switches the active model (a
`models.custom.<name>` switches provider+endpoint+model in one step);
`/models config` displays this section, `/models set <slot> <model>
[baseUrl]` and `/models remove <slot>` edit `models.slots`;
`/model-edit [contextWindow|maxTokens <n>]` overrides token limits for the
session (persist per chain via `roles:` entries instead) — bare in the TUI
it aliases into `/settings` → Model capabilities, the one surface that pins
`models.overrides` (issue #1515). Role edits apply at next boot; `/model`
applies live.

## Provider queue

Project or user file section; the `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var carries
the same JSON list and WINS over both files (issue #418). The ordered
failover chain replaces the main model: the first healthy entry serves,
a dead provider hands over loudly to the next, the winner sticks for
the session (RAM-only, never persisted), and cooled-down entries
re-enter rotation:

```yaml
providersQueue:
  - provider_type: openai-completions
    provider_config:
      model: moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6
      baseUrl: https://gate.example/v1
      apiKeyEnv: OPENAI_API_KEY
  - provider_type: anthropic
    provider_config:
      model: claude-sonnet-4-6
      apiKeyEnv: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
```

`apiKeyEnv` names the ENV indirection — a key VALUE never lives in the
yaml. CLI equivalent: `/providers queue list|add|remove|move|test`;
edits persist to the winning scope's file and go live from the next
turn. App Settings carries the same editor (env scope is read-only
there).

## Tool availability

<!-- parity: /tools -->

1. global — `~/.fah/config.yaml` `tools:`
2. project — `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` `tools:`
3. session — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` next to the session file

## Compaction

Context-hiding engine choice (issue #148). User or project file (project
wins):

```yaml
compaction:
  engine: structured           # structured (default) | classic (rollback)
```

`structured` (the default since issue #287) hides records in place behind
one-line addressable markers (`compact_expand` restores any id or range
under a per-turn token budget); `classic` keeps the lossy summary

`fa --compaction-engine classic`; resolution is
flag > project > global > the structured default. Applies at
the next compaction.

## Power

User file section (issue #325, reworked in #326). Sleep prevention for
live runs — by default ONE assertion PER RUN (acquired when the run
goes in flight, released when it settles), so the machine cannot
idle/sleep out from under a long run but CAN sleep while the agent
idles between turns:

```yaml
power:
  sleepPrevention: idle # off | idle | display | system (default idle)
  hold: per-run # per-run | session (default per-run)
```

Levels are cumulative: `idle` keeps the system from idle-sleeping
(macOS `caffeinate -i`), `display` also keeps the display awake
(`-i -d`), `system` also blocks AC system sleep and declares the user
active (`-i -d -s -u`). `hold: session` is the explicit opt-in that
holds from session start to exit instead (always-on deployments).
macOS spawns `caffeinate -w <fa pid>` (exits with fa — never
orphaned), Linux tries `systemd-inhibit` best-effort, other platforms
no-op. A failed assertion is a warning, never a crash.

CLI equivalent: `/power` (level + hold + held state). Applies at next
boot.

## Subagents heartbeat

User file section (issue #383). While a background subagent runs, the
parent receives a periodic status digest through the steering channel —
age, provider requests/tokens, last activity, and a
`healthy | stalled | no-progress-since-spawn` classification per running
child. A child with no provider activity for `stallMinutes` (or that
never issued a request at all) gets a loud `⚠ STALLED` flag with the
suggested `task_status → task_cancel → respawn` action; the flag
escalates to `⚠⚠` at twice the threshold:

```yaml
subagents:
  heartbeatMinutes: 10 # digests cadence; 0 disables the heartbeat
  stallMinutes: 20 # quiet window before a stall flag; 0 disables flags
  replyAutoSpill: true # oversized child replies auto-spill to an artifact
```

Zero running children → no digest; completion notices are unchanged.
Config changes apply at the next digest tick — no restart required.

`subagents.replyAutoSpill` (gh-1956, default `true`): an oversized child
`reply` spills to an artifact automatically — the parent receives a bounded
excerpt + `agent://` pointer + completeness marker instead of raw bytes, and
manual chunking degrades to a fallback. Set it to `false` to restore the
pure-chunk behavior (the child must chunk long reports manually).

## Theme

<!-- parity: /theme -->

The TUI palette is data, never code. `/theme` lists every available theme
(built-ins first, then user themes) with a swatch preview; `/theme <name>`
switches immediately and persists the choice; `/theme reset` returns to
the default.

Config equivalent — the persisted theme name:

```yaml
tui:
  theme: default   # a built-in name or a user theme file stem
```

Built-in names: `default` (the historical site palette — teal `#5eead4`,
indigo `#818cf8`), `catppuccin`, `nord`, `dracula`, `ohmypi-dark`,
`ohmypi-light`, `pi`.

User themes live in `~/.fah/themes/<name>.json`; the file stem is the
theme name, and a user theme can never shadow a built-in (a clashing file
name is skipped with a boot note). The JSON holds a `"roles"` object mapping ROLE names to hex colors
(`"#rgb"` or `"#rrggbb"`): `accent`, `accent2`, `muted`, `highlight`,
`success`, `warning`, `error`, `border`, `focusBorder`, `userMessageBg`.
Every role is optional — a missing role inherits the default theme for
that slot. Unknown role names, invalid hex, or broken JSON produce a
named error (file, role, line) at load time, never a crash.

Applies: `/theme <name>` switches the live session in one frame; a direct
YAML edit takes effect at next boot. Asked to create a theme from a
description, write the JSON file, then apply it with `/theme <name>` and
confirm the swatch line with the user. Asked for a palette "like X" where
X is unknown, ask two or three palette questions first — never invent one
silently.

### Compaction report detail

By default an auto-compaction fold prints ONE short marker line
(`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the internal
checkpoint summary stays in the session file (reachable via
`compact_expand`) and out of the console. To render the full report block
(records + fenced summary) and the live summarizer stream on headless
runs, opt in:

```yaml
tui:
  showCompactionDetails: true
```

The manual `/compact` command always renders the full block. Applies at
next boot.

The remaining user-file sections (all global scope):

```yaml
prompts:                        # prompt overrides: prompt id → text or @file
  concise: "Answer in one short paragraph."
ttsr:                           # tool-schema reduction (TTSR)
  enabled: true
  contextMode: keep             # keep | discard
  repeatMode: after-gap         # after-gap | once
```

## Output

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Console-output behavior flags (gh-1198 + gh-1433), user file. Today one
key — the live thinking stream for CLI line-mode runs: with
`streamThinking: true` (or the `--stream-thinking` flag, which wins for
the run), thinking deltas print dimmed and live like the TUI's, so ssh
sessions show the model's reasoning as it happens. The default `false`
keeps the interactive line-mode byte shape and prints a periodic
`… reasoning Ns` liveness line instead while a provider request sits
silent — the same waiting cadence the tool-liveness lines use
(`waiting.toolLivenessSeconds` / `toolLivenessTickSeconds`; `0` disables).

Since gh-1433 this key decides the INTERACTIVE faces only: a headless
`fa -p` run streams thinking and text by default (the log is the UI, no
flags needed). `--no-stream-thinking` silences thinking for one headless
run (the reasoning liveness line returns), and `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy`
reverts the whole headless face to the pre-gh-1433 byte shape for edge
hosts that parse the log. Rendered deltas — thinking AND streamed text,
on every face — pass through the redaction pipeline at render time since
gh-1433: a registered secret echoed in a delta is masked live, so
byte-pin tests for interactive `--stream-thinking` sessions must assume
redacted deltas whenever redaction is enabled (default).

```yaml
output:
  streamThinking: false # interactive line mode only; headless runs stream by default
```

Applies at next boot (the flag applies to its own run).

## Tool-result & user-message spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and
the session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678).
An oversized USER message (headless prompt, TUI input, steering) spills
to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/user-<n>.md` and the model receives a
bounded head+tail preview plus a read-in-parts instruction (issue
#1760). Tolerant parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as
`[spills]` notes at boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills — it beats the `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` /
`FAH_USER_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knobs too); `threshold: 0` disables
tool-result spilling only, `userThreshold: 0` the user path only:

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills; 0 = tools off
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
  userThreshold: 16384 # absolute byte floor for the user path; 0 = user off
  userFraction: 0.5 # spill a user message over this fraction of the live window budget
```

Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Project context budget

<!-- parity: notices on both surfaces; the byte knob is a config-file setting -->

`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md`/`GOAL.md`/`DESIGN.md` + Copilot
instruction files merge into the system prompt under a byte budget,
allocated leaf-first (deeper files win, issue #1761). Truncation is never
silent: the model sees a head excerpt plus an explicit
read-the-full-file instruction, a dropped file leaves a one-line
tombstone, and the user gets a boot notice per truncated/dropped file.
Tolerant parse: unknown keys surface as `[projectContext]` notes at boot,
never boot failures. `maxBytes: 0` disables the section entirely (no file
reads, fast boot):

```yaml
projectContext:
  maxBytes: 32768 # merged budget; 0 = section off, no file reads
```

Applies at next boot.

## Auto update

<!-- parity: /update, settings hub -->

User file top-level key (issue #1377). The self-update policy — a
tri-state, because the honest default is neither silent-off nor
unattended-on:

```yaml
auto_update: true # true | false | "notify" (default notify)
```

`notify` (the default) checks the release feed once at boot and prints
when a newer version exists — nothing is downloaded. `true` is the
unattended arm: at boot a newer release is downloaded, provenance
verified and installed, and the session restarts onto the new binary.
`false` touches no update host at all. An absent key and an explicit
`"notify"` are the same policy — the default is never written. Strict
parse: anything but `true`, `false` or `"notify"` is a
`ConfigException`. Applies at next boot. `/update` runs a check-and-apply
immediately regardless of the policy; the settings hub exposes the same
tri-state.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(#1947): `schedule_message` from the orchestrator no longer misroutes
  into a finished subagent's mailbox. A background shell job started by a
  CHILD registered its settle continuation inside the child's subagent
  zone; when the job settled after the child's run ended, the CLI's
  settle-wake (`_onShellJobSettled` → `_startRun`) started MAIN's reaction
  run still carrying the finished child's `activeSubagentId()`, and every
  identity consumer of that run misattributed it — the reported shape was
  a self-reminder scheduled "in <session>/<child>" that auto-resumed the
  completed child (duplicate-release risk). Three layers: the
  `ShellJobRegistry` now binds its settle continuation to the
  construction-time (boot) zone (`_bootZone.run`), both hosts'
  `scheduleSenderMailbox` wiring trusts the zone scope only while the
  child is genuinely in flight on the session executor
  (`TaskExecutor.isInFlight`), and the tool response names the RECIPIENT
  the record carries — an explicit `to:` used to be shadowed in the reply
  by the sender's mailbox, which read as "the override was ignored" even
  when it was honored. E2E repro drives the real AgentCli
  (test/cli/agent_cli_schedule_recipient_test.dart) plus a registry-level
  zone pin (test/tools/shell_job_settle_zone_test.dart).
- fix(gh-1948): `task_observe` works on a RUNNING background subagent
  instead of crashing with an uncaught `SessionException` on the
  `<parentSessionId>/<agentName>` placeholder. Three legs: the executor
  flushes each child's transcript incrementally at every turn boundary
  (the JSONL exists and grows mid-run — also crash-resilience for
  aborted children), `task_observe` resolves a placeholder handle's real
  session file from the sessions tree (the same `agent: subagent` /
  `parent:` / `id:` header scan the boot adoption uses) and heals the
  handle onto the found path, and every read failure degrades to a
  structured "transcript unavailable" / "no transcript available yet"
  message instead of an uncaught tool error. The child-transcript reader
  rides the transient-ENOENT retry (issue #427) — it reads while the
  executor appends.
- fix(#1941): the selected CodeMie project now rides EVERY model request.
  The header is baked into `Model.headers` only by the connect-time
  switches (gh-1809), so every other rebuild silently dropped
  `x-codemie-project` — and the backend bills a header-less request against
  the user's DEFAULT project (codemie-code `header-injection.plugin.ts`
  contract): the reported symptom is limit-exhausted from the exhausted

## Unreleased

- feat(gh-1956): reply auto-spill — oversized child `reply` / `agent_message`
  payloads spill to an `agent://` artifact automatically; the parent receives a
  bounded excerpt + pointer + completeness marker with char AND byte counts.
  Manual chunking degrades to a documented fallback, restorable across parent
  resume via durable `deliverable_artifact` records, behind the

  the app host alike). Rework round: the salvage hook (output-truncated
  deliverable calls) restores the durable ids before allocating its own

# Re: ⚠️ IMPORTANT — the truncated-call salvage hook skips the restore

**Fixed** — the invariant is now true for every id-allocating path.

`captureSalvaged` (`lib/src/task/deliverables.dart`) is now `Future<void>` and awaits the memoized `ensureRestored()` BEFORE the `_persist` id allocation, exactly as suggested. Since the hook is now awaited end-to-end, the plumbing changed type:

- `Agent.onTruncatedToolCall` and `AgentLoopConfig.onTruncatedToolCall` are `Future<void> Function(ToolCall call)?`.
- The loop (`agent_loop.dart`, `_failToolCallsFromTruncatedMessage`) awaits the hook before emitting the truncation failure — a nice side effect: the salvage artifact is persisted before the failure tool-result (and any tier-2 pointer note) is emitted.
- `TaskExecutor`'s two wiring sites (`task_executor.dart:925` / `:1200`) await `_capture?.captureSalvaged(...)` in the closure.

The race shape from the thread is covered by a regression test: `test/task/reply_auto_spill_test.dart` → *"the salvage hook restores durable rows before allocating an id"* — a pending `restoreArtifacts` future holding the `kid-report` row races a truncated `reply` salvage; with the fix the salvaged partial artifact gets a distinct id and the durable content survives `store.get('kid-report')` unchanged (before the fix the salvage allocated `kid-report` first and the first-write-wins restore silently dropped the durable row — the test reproduces exactly that ordering).

# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION — the byte count is re-encoded up to 4× per spill

**Fixed** — computed once at the `_persist` boundary and threaded through, as suggested. Pure refactor; all byte-count and envelope tests pass unchanged.

`lib/src/task/deliverables.dart`:

- `_persist` computes `final bytes = utf8.encode(redacted).length` once, directly after the id allocation, and reuses it for the fit-check overhead, `AgentArtifactMeta.bytes`, the returned `DeliverableRecord`, and the durable row's implicit content — no other full encode of the artifact text remains on the spill path.
- `_statusLine` now takes the precomputed `int bytes` instead of the `String stored` body (its per-branch `utf8.encode(stored).length` encodes are gone); both the `_persist` fit check and `envelopeText` pass it in.
- `envelopeText` reads `record.bytes` (the capture always supplies it) with a single-encode fallback for a legacy externally-built record.
- On the restore path `_runRestore` already encoded once per row — unchanged.

Net effect for the 100 KB+ payload class this feature targets: ~3–4 O(n) encodes per delivery → 1 (plus 1 on restore).

# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION — hand-pinned calibration constants will re-break this test

**Fixed** — both suggested hardenings applied in `test/task/subagent_compaction_test.dart`, with one deliberate deviation on the guard operator (explained below).

**Derivation split (suggestion 1, adapted):** the baseline can't be fully derived from `taskReportSizeContractPrompt.length` because the two tool-description sizes are hand-written Dart literals in `subagent_tools.dart`, not generated constants — deriving them would just move the pin. So the baseline is SPLIT so the brittle half self-heals:

- the CONTRACT term derives from the shipped prompt constant (`deliverableChunkContract(8000).length`; gh-1956 measured 948 at budget 800) — a future edit to `report_size_contract.md` re-baselines itself and no longer needs a recalibration here;
- the gh-1956 tool-description sizes stay PINNED with provenance in the `_gh1956BaselineChars` doc (reply 592 + agent_message 799, pointing at the REPORT SIZE paragraphs in `_replyTool`/`_agentMessageTool`), so a description edit lands as a one-line diff.

**Baseline assertion (suggestion 2):** a new calibration guard group asserts `expect(_childFootprintChars, greaterThanOrEqualTo(_gh1956BaselineChars))` — the footprint computation is hoisted into a named `_childFootprintChars` getter shared by `_contractTokens` and the guard, so the two can't drift apart. I used `greaterThanOrEqualTo` rather than the suggested `greaterThan` because exact equality IS the calibrated gh-1956 point (today's footprint equals the baseline); `greaterThan` would fail on the very commit that pins the baseline. The guard catches the dangerous direction — a shrink below baseline, which would push the delta term negative and silently widen the fixture windows.

The provenance comment in `_contractTokens` now also names the 237 offset as the pre-gh-1956 contract footprint in tokens.

`DeliverableRecord.artifact` (`lib/src/task/deliverables.dart`): `required this.bytes` → `this.bytes`. The doc now states the compatibility contract explicitly: the barrel-exported type is published package API, so gh-1956 must not break out-of-repo constructors; the harness-owned spill path (`_persist`) always supplies the byte count, legacy external callers simply render chars-only.

`_renderArtifact` handles the null gracefully — `(N chars)` without the byte segment, for both the per-part and plain artifact render forms; spill-produced records are byte-identical to before (`(N chars, M bytes)`).

# gh-1956 rework — review round 1: all 8 open threads closed

## Issues/Notes

- **CI at rework start was green** (`ci_failures.md`: no failed checks, no owned-violations table) — this pass is review-thread fixes only; no owned CI violations to list.
- An in-progress `origin/main` merge found on the branch at rework start was conflict-free and concluded first (`git diff --check` clean, no markers), so all fixes land on top of current main (689456671c).
- **Pre-existing breakage (not from this PR, not chased):** `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` (documented in the PR description — fails on clean `origin/main` too) plus sandbox-environment PTY tests (`pty_resume_equivalence_test.dart`, `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test.dart`) that spawn real pseudo-terminals. Their pre-existing status on the merge-base is verified in the rework log. Untouched by this pass.
- Branch housekeeping: the harness's 5-minute WIP auto-save had pushed three snapshot commits (one carrying a whole-tree formatter churn from an SDK-format mismatch — this repo's CI has no `dart format` gate). The churn was reverted and the snapshots were folded back via an `ours`-strategy merge; the PR delta vs `main` contains exactly the feature files + this round's 17 changed files.
- The rework commit also adds the repo-conventional `feat(gh-1956)` `## Unreleased` CHANGELOG entry (flagged by the automated review).

## Approach

Three IMPORTANT threads first (TDD: each fix preceded by a failing test), then the five suggestions:

1. **Salvage hook skips the restore (invariant hole)** — `captureSalvaged` is now `Future<void>`, awaits the memoized `ensureRestored()` before its id-allocating `_persist`, and is awaited end-to-end (`Agent.onTruncatedToolCall` / `AgentLoopConfig.onTruncatedToolCall` → `Future<void> Function(ToolCall)?`; the loop awaits before emitting the truncation failure; both `TaskExecutor` wiring sites await the capture). RED: a pending-restore race test — with the old code the salvage allocated `kid-report` first and the first-write-wins restore silently dropped the durable content; with the fix the restored row keeps its id and the salvaged partial gets a distinct id.
2. **Kill switch dead on non-CLI hosts** — `AppFahSections` now parses the `subagents:` section with the CLI's own `SubagentsConfig.fromYaml` (AC7: malformed → named warning + defaults); `AgentService` hands `appConfig?.subagents` to the app builder, which wires `replyAutoSpill: () => subagentsConfig?.replyAutoSpill ?? defaultReplyAutoSpill` into `SubagentServices`. `subagents.replyAutoSpill: false` now behaves identically on the CLI and the app; the doc ("any host") is true as written. RED: section-parse + CLI/app parity-guard tests.
3. **Silent durability failures** — new `deliverableDurabilityLog` host sink (the `deliverySloSink`/`connTraceStderrSink` convention): `_persistRow`'s `catchError` emits `[deliverables] artifact persist failed: <error>`; the CLI sink's null-session early return emits a dropped-row line; the CLI io root (`_wireDeliverableDurabilityLog`, wired at boot + `wireRunNoticesForTesting`) routes every line to fa.log AND a dim transcript line. RED: throwing-sink diagnostic test + silence-by-default test + CLI wiring pin.
4. `spillApliesTo` → `spillAppliesTo` (barrel-exported public API; one call site in `subagent_tools.dart`). RED: public-name API test.
5. Byte count computed once per spill at the `_persist` boundary; threaded into the fit check, `AgentArtifactMeta`, the record, and `_statusLine` (now takes `int bytes`); `envelopeText` reads `record.bytes` with a single-encode fallback. Pure refactor — every byte-count/envelope test unchanged.
6. Dead ternary in the `_toolsRig` test rig simplified to `capture ?? effective`.
7. Compaction-test calibration hardened: the contract term of the baseline derives from the shipped `report_size_contract.md` constant (a prompt-copy edit re-baselines itself); the gh-1956 tool-description sizes (592/799) stay pinned with provenance pointing at the `subagent_tools.dart` paragraphs; the footprint is hoisted into a shared `_childFootprintChars` getter and a guard test asserts it never drifts below the baseline (`greaterThanOrEqualTo` — equality IS the calibrated gh-1956 point, so the reviewer's literal `greaterThan` would fail on the pinning commit itself).
8. `DeliverableRecord.artifact(bytes)` is optional again (published-package constructor compat); null renders chars-only, spill-produced records render unchanged. RED: a compile-failing legacy-constructor test. Plus the `feat(gh-1956)` CHANGELOG entry.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/task/deliverables.dart` — async `captureSalvaged` + restore-before-persist; `deliverableDurabilityLog` sink + diagnostic in `_persistRow`; `spillAppliesTo` rename; single-encode `bytes` threading (`_persist`, `_statusLine`, `envelopeText`); optional `bytes` + null-safe `_renderArtifact`.
- `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`, `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — `onTruncatedToolCall` hook type → `Future<void> Function(ToolCall)?`, awaited at the truncation-failure site.
- `lib/src/task/task_executor.dart` — both salvage wiring closures await the capture.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — durability line on the sink's null-session early return; io-root durability wiring called at boot.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` — `_wireDeliverableDurabilityLog()` (fa.log + dim transcript line), added to the boot wiring and `wireRunNoticesForTesting`.
- `lib/src/config/app_config_sections.dart` — `AppFahSections.subagents` parsed via `SubagentsConfig.fromYaml` (AC7 warning-on-bad).
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`, `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_host_builder.dart` — the app host wires `replyAutoSpill` from the parsed section.
- `lib/src/task/subagent_tools.dart` — renamed `spillAppliesTo` call site.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `feat(gh-1956)` Unreleased entry.
- Tests: `test/task/reply_auto_spill_test.dart` (race repro, durability diagnostics, spill-gate public-name test, legacy-constructor compat, dead ternary), `test/task/deliverables_test.dart` (awaited salvage calls), `test/agent/agent_loop_truncated_capture_test.dart` (async hook), `test/cli/agent_cli_run_notices_test.dart` (durability sink wiring), `test/config/app_config_sections_test.dart` (subagents parse group), `test/config/app_cli_config_parity_test.dart` (subagents parity), `test/task/subagent_compaction_test.dart` (calibration provenance + guard).

## Test Coverage

- `dart analyze`: no issues in any changed file (remaining office_addin resolution errors are pre-existing environment noise in an untouched sub-package). Changed Dart files are format-clean under the sandbox SDK; the repo's CI has no format gate.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.

# gh-1956 rework — review round 1: all 8 open threads closed

## Issues/Notes

- **CI at rework start was green** (`ci_failures.md`: no failed checks, no owned-violations table) — this pass is review-thread fixes only; no owned CI violations to list.
- An in-progress `origin/main` merge found on the branch at rework start was conflict-free and concluded first (`git diff --check` clean, no markers), so all fixes land on top of current main (689456671c).
- **Pre-existing breakage (not from this PR, not chased):** `test/integration/backend_mode_cli_test.dart` (documented in the PR description — fails on clean `origin/main` too) plus sandbox-environment PTY tests (`pty_resume_equivalence_test.dart`, `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test.dart`) that spawn real pseudo-terminals. Their pre-existing status on the merge-base is verified in the rework log. Untouched by this pass.
- Branch housekeeping: the harness's 5-minute WIP auto-save had pushed three snapshot commits (one carrying a whole-tree formatter churn from an SDK-format mismatch — this repo's CI has no `dart format` gate). The churn was reverted and the snapshots were folded back via an `ours`-strategy merge; the PR delta vs `main` contains exactly the feature files + this round's 17 changed files.
- The rework commit also adds the repo-conventional `feat(gh-1956)` `## Unreleased` CHANGELOG entry (flagged by the automated review).

## Approach

Three IMPORTANT threads first (TDD: each fix preceded by a failing test), then the five suggestions:

1. **Salvage hook skips the restore (invariant hole)** — `captureSalvaged` is now `Future<void>`, awaits the memoized `ensureRestored()` before its id-allocating `_persist`, and is awaited end-to-end (`Agent.onTruncatedToolCall` / `AgentLoopConfig.onTruncatedToolCall` → `Future<void> Function(ToolCall)?`; the loop awaits before emitting the truncation failure; both `TaskExecutor` wiring sites await the capture). RED: a pending-restore race test — with the old code the salvage allocated `kid-report` first and the first-write-wins restore silently dropped the durable content; with the fix the restored row keeps its id and the salvaged partial gets a distinct id.
2. **Kill switch dead on non-CLI hosts** — `AppFahSections` now parses the `subagents:` section with the CLI's own `SubagentsConfig.fromYaml` (AC7: malformed → named warning + defaults); `AgentService` hands `appConfig?.subagents` to the app builder, which wires `replyAutoSpill: () => subagentsConfig?.replyAutoSpill ?? defaultReplyAutoSpill` into `SubagentServices`. `subagents.replyAutoSpill: false` now behaves identically on the CLI and the app; the doc ("any host") is true as written. RED: section-parse + CLI/app parity-guard tests.
3. **Silent durability failures** — new `deliverableDurabilityLog` host sink (the `deliverySloSink`/`connTraceStderrSink` convention): `_persistRow`'s `catchError` emits `[deliverables] artifact persist failed: <error>`; the CLI sink's null-session early return emits a dropped-row line; the CLI io root (`_wireDeliverableDurabilityLog`, wired at boot + `wireRunNoticesForTesting`) routes every line to fa.log AND a dim transcript line. RED: throwing-sink diagnostic test + silence-by-default test + CLI wiring pin.
4. `spillApliesTo` → `spillAppliesTo` (barrel-exported public API; one call site in `subagent_tools.dart`). RED: public-name API test.
5. Byte count computed once per spill at the `_persist` boundary; threaded into the fit check, `AgentArtifactMeta`, the record, and `_statusLine` (now takes `int bytes`); `envelopeText` reads `record.bytes` with a single-encode fallback. Pure refactor — every byte-count/envelope test unchanged.
6. Dead ternary in the `_toolsRig` test rig simplified to `capture ?? effective`.
7. Compaction-test calibration hardened: the contract term of the baseline derives from the shipped `report_size_contract.md` constant (a prompt-copy edit re-baselines itself); the gh-1956 tool-description sizes (592/799) stay pinned with provenance pointing at the `subagent_tools.dart` paragraphs; the footprint is hoisted into a shared `_childFootprintChars` getter and a guard test asserts it never drifts below the baseline (`greaterThanOrEqualTo` — equality IS the calibrated gh-1956 point, so the reviewer's literal `greaterThan` would fail on the pinning commit itself).
8. `DeliverableRecord.artifact(bytes)` is optional again (published-package constructor compat); null renders chars-only, spill-produced records render unchanged. RED: a compile-failing legacy-constructor test. Plus the `feat(gh-1956)` CHANGELOG entry.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/task/deliverables.dart` — async `captureSalvaged` + restore-before-persist; `deliverableDurabilityLog` sink + diagnostic in `_persistRow`; `spillAppliesTo` rename; single-encode `bytes` threading (`_persist`, `_statusLine`, `envelopeText`); optional `bytes` + null-safe `_renderArtifact`.
- `lib/src/agent/agent.dart`, `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — `onTruncatedToolCall` hook type → `Future<void> Function(ToolCall)?`, awaited at the truncation-failure site.
- `lib/src/task/task_executor.dart` — both salvage wiring closures await the capture.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — durability line on the sink's null-session early return; io-root durability wiring called at boot.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` — `_wireDeliverableDurabilityLog()` (fa.log + dim transcript line), added to the boot wiring and `wireRunNoticesForTesting`.
- `lib/src/config/app_config_sections.dart` — `AppFahSections.subagents` parsed via `SubagentsConfig.fromYaml` (AC7 warning-on-bad).
- `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart`, `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service_host_builder.dart` — the app host wires `replyAutoSpill` from the parsed section.
- `lib/src/task/subagent_tools.dart` — renamed `spillAppliesTo` call site.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `feat(gh-1956)` Unreleased entry.
